group.title: Daily routine
group.tagline: Your day from morning to night
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To clean teeth or make hair neat with a tool that has many hairs.
wrong: I brush my teeth with a spoon of sugar to make them dirty.

words.meaning: A small tool you use to clean your teeth.
wrong: I comb the dog’s hair with my toothbrush and eat soup with it.

words.meaning: Soft paste you put on a brush to clean your teeth.
examples: Put a little {toothpaste} on your brush.
wrong: I put toothpaste on my bread for lunch.

words.meaning: A flat tool with thin teeth that makes your hair neat.
examples: She keeps a {comb} in her bag.
wrong: I eat my rice with a comb.

words.meaning: A brush you use to make your hair tidy.
wrong: I clean my teeth with my hairbrush.

words.meaning: To put your clothes on.
wrong: I get dressed by taking all my clothes off.

words.meaning: To wash your body under falling water.
wrong: I take a shower and stay totally dry.

words.meaning: To eat the first meal of the day.
wrong: I have breakfast just before I go to bed at night.

words.meaning: To lie down to sleep at night.
examples: The children {go to bed} at eight.
wrong: I go to bed when I wake up in the morning.

words.meaning: To travel to the place where you have your job.
examples: My dad {goes to work} by bus.
wrong: She goes to work, so she stays home all day.

words.meaning: To travel to school or be a student there.
examples: I {go to school} at eight o’clock.
wrong: My baby brother goes to school, but he is one month old.

words.meaning: To travel back to the place where you live.
examples: After work, I {go home} and rest.
wrong: I go home to a hotel I have never seen.

words.meaning: A clock that makes a loud noise to wake you up.
wrong: My alarm clock helps me fall asleep.

words.meaning: To cut hair off your face or body with a sharp tool.
wrong: He shaved his beard, so now it is very long.

words.meaning: To put the sheets and blankets on a bed neatly.
examples: I {make the bed} after I get up.
wrong: I make the bed by throwing the blankets on the floor.

words.meaning: The part of the day after twelve and before evening.
wrong: I have breakfast at seven in the afternoon.

words.meaning: On all the days, again and again.
wrong: I go to school every day, but only on Mondays.

words.meaning: Not sleeping.
examples: I am {awake} at six every morning.
wrong: He was awake, so his eyes were closed and he was dreaming.

words.meaning: Sleeping.
examples: The baby is {asleep} in her bed.
wrong: She is asleep and talking on the phone.

words.meaning: In the early part of the day.
wrong: I see the moon and stars in the morning sun.

words.meaning: Thirty minutes after the hour.
wrong: Half past eight is ten minutes after eight.

words.meaning: To start sleeping.
examples: I {go to sleep} at ten o’clock.
wrong: I go to sleep and play soccer all night.

words.meaning: To eat the meal in the middle of the day.
wrong: I have lunch at six in the morning before breakfast.

words.meaning: Pictures and stories in your head when you sleep.
examples: I had a {dream} about a big dog.
wrong: I had a dream while I was awake at my desk.

words.meaning: The time when you go to bed.
wrong: Bedtime is when I wake up in the morning.

words.meaning: The time in the middle of the day when people eat.
wrong: Lunchtime is at midnight.

words.meaning: To make yourself ready to go somewhere.
examples: I {get ready} for school in ten minutes.
wrong: I get ready for school by going back to sleep.

words.meaning: To go out of your home.
examples: I {leave the house} at seven thirty.
wrong: I leave the house and stay inside all day.

words.meaning: Next, at a later time.
examples: I eat breakfast. {After that}, I go to school.
wrong: After that means the thing that happened first.

words.meaning: Any day from Monday to Friday.
wrong: Sunday is my favorite weekday.

words.meaning: Soft clothes you wear in bed.
examples: I put on my {pajamas} at night.
wrong: He wears pajamas to swim in the sea.

words.meaning: To take water off something.
examples: I {dry} my hair with a towel.
wrong: I dry my hands by putting them in water.

words.meaning: Fifteen minutes after the hour.
wrong: Quarter past six is half an hour after six.

words.meaning: A day when you do not have to work.
wrong: On my day off I work for twelve hours.

words.meaning: Soft shoes you wear in the house.
wrong: I wear my slippers to climb mountains in the snow.

words.meaning: To take your dog outside for a walk.
wrong: I walk the dog by leaving it in a box all day.

words.meaning: To give food to a person or animal.
wrong: I feed the fish by taking all its food away.

words.meaning: A small clock you wear on your wrist.
examples: My {watch} says it is eight o’clock.
wrong: I wear my watch on my nose.

words.meaning: A short time in the middle of the day to stop work and eat.
examples: I have a sandwich on my {lunch break}.
wrong: My lunch break is the longest part of the work day.

words.meaning: To arrive at the place where you live.
examples: I {get home} at six in the evening.
wrong: I get home, so I am far away from my house.
